source_issue.summary: Unify Green color, transparency and border color of all green UI elements
source_issue.description:
Most green elements are slightly translucent and have a bright green border around them. 

* The tensioner force bar does not include a bright green border since the colors of the bar change from green --> red --> green often. this was found to be distracting.

* Other such green UI elements (non-stressed ROM collection) don't have changing colors. They go from 'not collected' to 'collected' and cannot be fluctuate between the two states.

Need to unify the color scheme for such elements.

source_issue.description:
+*FEATURE DESCRIPTION & INCLUDES*+

* Ability to visualize and plan for placement of augments.
* Separate augment planning stage upon completion of implant planning with gaps.
* Distinctly show augments on-screen.
* Initial augment sizing to be based on maximum thickness of bone loss.
* Orthogonal view
* 3D view and cross-section view modes
* Ability to modify augment size
* Other options widget (similar to combined planning)
* Rotate view
* Implant on/off view mode
* Maximize, minimize view
* Regular widgets: screenshot, shutdown, checkpoints, info widget

+*CONTEXT*+
In this state, the surgeon fills up the bone loss by using augments. There are two augments for the femur and two for the tibia.



+*BENEFIT HYPOTHESIS*+

+*ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA*+

*  Stage appears upon completion of combined planning with (or without in measured resection cases) gaps
* System identifies the minimum normal distance (greater than zero) of the refined surface vertices from the distal origin and posterior origin of the implant cutplanes. 
* System assigns the minimum augment size needed to fill up this bone loss.
* Ability to modify augments
* Visualize in 3D and cross-section view modes

+*ARCHITECTURAL RUNWAY NEEDS*+

 

+*REFERENCES*+

# ER0665
# Prolaborate Feature Definition Diagram link :[https://prolaborate.sncloudcontrol.com/LmCqqG|https://prolaborate.sncloudcontrol.com/LmCqqG|smart-link] 

+*OPEN QUESTIONS*+

# Are there any user notifications that are applicable?
# Do we need cut bone view?

source_issue.description:
+*FEATURE DESCRIPTION*+

The user requires a means to enable the features associated with the purchased feature set for revision knee replacement, and then use those features within a revision case.

+*CONTEXT*+

+*INCLUDES:*+

Means to enable features associated with revision knee procedure, upon installation:

# Means to enable the feature set (akin to total knee features enabling)
# Means to confirm user has purchased the feature set (additional line in code)
# Means to install Revision Implant (LEGION RK, plus augments) via the terminal.

Means to include enabled features in case workflow for Revision Procedures:

# (1)   Case Creation Screen
## Procedure: TKA
## Implant: LEGION RK
#    Surgeon Preferences Screen
##  Joint Laxity: Collect / Skip
## Initial Implant Planning: Yes / No
## Femur Rotational Reference: PCA / Manually Define
## Tibia Resection: Default / +1 /+2 / +3
## Femur Implant Referencing : Anterior  / Posterior
## SDIP: Yes / No – TBD how implemented
## Rotation Center (Femur): Medial Posterior / Knee Center
## Femur Cut Selection: Distal Bur / Bur all
## Joint Line: Femur / Tibia / Both / None

All preferences are available for all procedures.

Selection of LEGION RK implant drives inclusion of Bone Refinement (F/T) between initial implant planning and gap assessment. 
Upon leaving implant planning, system will read last implant selected, should it be LEGION RK, Augment Planning will appear.

If features are enabled, all should be accessed from Other Options button (joint line, refinement, augment planning).

If you change implants from TKA to RK, system will prompt user to complete bone refinement stages.

+*BENEFIT HYPOTHESIS*+

# Enabling features allows the surgeon to access features needed for a revision knee procedure.
# Enabling features allows the business to have a means to track enabling of these features to a purchase.

+*ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA*+

# Enabling of features is not more steps / procedures that are required for system installation or updates, as it stands today
# Enabling procedures does not create a separate procedure code.

 

+*ARCHITECTURAL RUNWAY NEEDS*+

 

+*REFERENCES*+

#  

+*OPEN QUESTIONS*+

source_issue.description:
+*FEATURE DESCRIPTION*+
This feature describes a need to create a surface which approximates the post explant bone surface. The post-explant bone surface needs to be referenced during planning and also needs to be used to create a volumentric cutting model for bone removal.

+*CONTEXT*+
This feature is needed for addition of RKA functionality. Upon completion of point collection in free collection, the software needs to create a volumetric model that can be refined to depict the surface of the bone once the original implant is removed. This will be used during planning to visualize. The screen will be combined with the gap planning state rather than right after the free collection state. - *Confirm post workflow discussions*
This has a dependency on the hardware that will be used to refine: using the CORI handpiece to refine or using the CORI pointer probe with a new refining guard.

Similar to the bone refinement stage in F/T bone removal, however, we need to have this stage prior to planning.

+*INCLUDES*+


# Creation of a volumetric model upon collection of sufficient free collection points.
# Potentially select tool used for refining or determine based on proximity to the bone.
# Allow for refining using handpiece
# Allow also for refining using the pointer probe \[Need to connect with the HW team to get the dimensions]
# 


+*BENEFIT HYPOTHESIS*+

Provides ability to characterize the bone without the primary implant on the surface.

To be used to visualize and plan for placement of RKA imlpant and Augments

+*ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA*+
The surgeon is able to create a surface representation of the post-explant bone surface. That surface is visible in planning. That surface can be made into a volumetric cutting model to be burred in bone removal.



+*ARCHITECTURAL RUNWAY NEEDS*+

* Add new surface/ cut model to datastore



+*REFERENCES*+
 

# See current bone refinement stage in bone removal
# Prolaborate Link: [https://prolaborate.sncloudcon...|https://prolaborate.sncloudcontrol.com/AUQl]
# [https://smith-nephew.atlassian.net/browse/CORI-15|https://smith-nephew.atlassian.net/browse/CORI-15|smart-link] 


+*OPEN QUESTIONS*+
 

# Should it be an option / mode from Femur free collection? Activated after atleast 25 points are collected in free collection. Benefits of doing this: It can always be an option in TKA.
# Can this be a push/pop navigation from planning? Benefits: reduces the number of times that the surgeon needs to take the primary implant on and off of the bone while keeping the TKA gap assessment stage where it is in the workflow. Risks: initial planning stage has no information about post-explant bone surface which is the primary surface referenced in RKA Planning.
# Should it be between gap assessment and planning with gaps?
# Or should it be a new stage right before planning similar to ER0665
#

source_issue.description:
+*FEATURE DESCRIPTION*+
This feature is to determine a method on how to store augments in the IDB generically, as well as develop all of the possible augments for the Legion family and put them in the IDB. This scope of work will include:

* Updates to the Q00040 process to gather design inputs for Revision type implant designs
* Updates to the IDB creator tools to support build and verification of Revision type implant designs
* Execution of the Q00040 process for revision type implant designs.

+*CONTEXT*+
Augments are metal "wedges" that are used to shim the implant where the bone is degraded and direct contact with the implant can not be made. The Augements come in various sizes and screw onto the implant, so the resulting available configurations of implant/augment constructions can be very numerous.  

+*BENEFIT HYPOTHESIS*+
Augments are needed for the RKA function to work, this feature is therefore must have.

+*ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA*+


# New project number has been created in DCS/Records/IDB Projects
# The following artifacts are completed and stored here:
# FM0129
# IDBInspectionDocument
# FM0049
# Following records are stored in Doc Control:
# CAD files
# Import group meeting minutes
# New IDB build is complete and installed on AccuCut laptop which includes changes to:
# New TKAAugmentsVerifier → PSDR created, validated
# Changes to IDBCreator
# Changes to IDBMerger
# NavioIDBInstaller2 updated
# New 910104.iso file created with ability to automatically install the Augments
# Update to Q40:
# Q40 - Released
# WI0013
# WI0014
# Release of IDB Requirements
# 


+*ARCHITECTURAL RUNWAY NEEDS*+

# Generic IDB Update to handle augments
# IDB applications needed for generating surfaces, cut angles, etc
# 


+*REFERENCES*+

# Q40
# WI0013
# WI0014
# Prolaborate Link: [https://prolaborate.sncloudcon...|https://prolaborate.sncloudcontrol.com/LhKcbR]
# 


+*OPEN QUESTIONS*+

# Will the current IDB process work?
# Can Augmentation be added generically to the IDB?
#

source_issue.description:
+*FEATURE DESCRIPTION*+
This feature is to use CORI to define the landmarks, measurements, and project the native femoral joint line during the registration process while the old implant is still attached. This feature includes the necessary stories to define the femoral joint line and support increasing the joint line distance from any landmarks to a point the surgeon deems appropriate.

The joint line will be calculated by CORI and rendered in CORI's UI on the bone mesh so that the surgeon can make a judgement if the line is in the appropriate place. The landmark point could be put in any location, the surgeon choose on the anatomy and the joint line should be calculated some distance away. This distance could be based upon a research papers that say 25mm on average is a good value or based upon the surgeon setting the value in OR from anatomical considerations. This requires some widget to be able to move the joint line up and down from CORI's measures or predicted location.

+*CONTEXT*+
The identification of the "native" or original joint line with the implant still on the patient is key to planning where the new implant should be placed. There are several methods for establishing the native joint line, one is to identify the femur joint line based upon landmarks during the registration process.

The first point corresponds to a clinical landmark. The second point is more of a convience so that the surgeon doesn’t have to use the toggle and click "lots of times". This method preserves flexibility for the variations in clinical selection of the landmarks.

+*BENEFIT HYPOTHESIS*+
One key goal in all RKA procedures is the restoration of the joint line of the knee, without feature this the application would have significantly reduced value.
